title: Diabetes emergencies in the hospital: DKA, HHS and hypoglycemia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's diabetes (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Hyperglycemia

Vitals:
BP: 138/84
HR: 76 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 96% on RA
Weight: 152 lbs

Recent Labs:
Glucose: 412 mg/dL (on admission)
HbA1c: 8.4%
Na: 138
K: 4.2
Cr: 0.9
eGFR: >90

Review of Systems:
(+) Polydipsia, polyuria. (-) Chest pain, SOB, syncope, numbness, vision changes.

Social History:
Lives with daughter. Retired. No tobacco use.

Family History:
Mother had type 2 diabetes. Father had HTN.

Hospital Course:
Pt is an 85-year-old female with a known hx of T2DM admitted with severe hyperglycemia. On admission, BG was >400 mg/dL. Pt was stable and did not meet criteria for acute metabolic crises. Management focused on fluid resuscitation and insulin adjustment. Pt responded well to sliding scale insulin and dose titration. BG stabilized within target range during stay. Diet was adjusted to consistent carb counts. Pt tolerated oral intake well and was ready for discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Hyperglycemia
2. Type 2 diabetes

Discharge Medications:
1. Metformin 500mg BID
2. Lisinopril 10mg daily
3. Atorvastatin 20mg daily
4. Insulin glargine and lispro as directed

Follow-up:
F/u with PCP in 1 week for lab work and medication reconciliation.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, MD
05/15/2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes with hyperglycemia only: E11.65 (HCC 38).
